issues.description: The template's Stock.findStockIngredient method has the signature findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive), while the problem statement UML and the solution expect a single-parameter method findStockIngredient(String). This mismatch causes compilation issues because other methods in the template (add, take) call findStockIngredient(String) and the intended SealSaloon and tests also call findStockIngredient(String).
issues.suggestedFix: Provide the single-argument method findStockIngredient(String name) in the template (or change the existing declaration to the single-argument form) so it matches the UML and solution. For example, add an overload: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) { return findStockIngredient(name, true); } or change the existing method to the single-parameter signature used by the problem and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect Stock.findStockIngredient(String) but the template's Stock implementation provides findStockIngredient(String, boolean caseSensitive). This mismatch in the method signature (extra parameter) creates confusion for students: the UML and instructions reference a single-argument method, example usages in Main call findStockIngredient(String), and the solution implements the single-argument form. The template's different signature prevents a clear mapping from the problem requirements to the starter code and will lead to compilation/usage errors or extra cognitive load as students try to reconcile the API difference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the problem statement and solution by providing findStockIngredient(String name) (single-argument). Either change the existing method signature to remove the boolean parameter or add an overloaded convenience method findStockIngredient(String name) that delegates to the case-sensitive variant with a sensible default. Ensure example usages (e.g., Main) compile against the single-argument method.
